newsitem.title: USA: Burst pipe shuts 2 MW Vermont hydropower plant.
newsitem.headline: Burst pipe shuts 2 MW Vermont hydropower plant.

text.p: A small hydroelectric power station in southern Vermont is expected to stay shut for several months after a water pipe burst Wednesday, said owner and operator Central Vermont Public Service Co.
"It's going to be several months worth of work," said company spokesman Steve Costello.
The two megawatt (MW) Glen hydro power plant in Rutland, Vt., would likely restart in late May or early June, he said.
The outage would not affect power supplies to customers, he said.
"We have plenty of excess power right now," Costello said, adding Glen accounts for less than one percent of the company's electricity output.
The incident occurred when plant workers were repairing a small leak on the three-quarter mile long pipe that carries water from a nearby dam.
